title: Social issues in information systems
competency: Explain the social benefits and problems of information systems: socialization gaps, cyberbullying, addiction, plagiarism, cybercrime and jobs.

keywords.def: The gap between people who have access to technology and those who do not.
Less natural interaction in families and among friends because each person is busy with a device.
Sending, posting or spreading hurtful or malicious content about someone online, or disclosing their private information to humiliate them.
A behavioural addiction: too much concern for social media or games, an urge to log on, and so much time spent that other life areas suffer.
Presenting work or ideas from another source as your own, with or without consent, without full acknowledgement.
Using a computer as an instrument for illegal ends, such as fraud, stealing identities or violating privacy and intellectual property rights.
A well-trained, skilled IT or information security professional who manages computer networks and system operations.
Using machines and systems to do routine tasks that people used to do.

ideas.name: Social benefits, socialization gaps, cyberbullying and addiction

en.text: Information systems bring social benefits: access to knowledge, a narrower digital divide, AI and augmented reality, and platforms for business and entertainment. They also cause problems. Socialization gaps appear when family members and friends each stare at their own device. Cyberbullying is posting or spreading hurtful content or private information about someone online. Social media and gaming addiction takes so much time that it harms other important areas of life.

am.text: ቴክኖሎጂ ጥቅም አለው፤ ግን የቤተሰብ ግንኙነት ክፍተት፣ የሳይበር ጉልበተኝነት እና የማኅበራዊ ሚዲያ ሱስ ያስከትላል።

screens.title: Good or harmful?
items: Online lessons reach students in rural areas
At dinner each family member stares at a phone
Posting an embarrassing photo of a classmate

screens.title: Social benefits
paras: Computers and the Internet give access to a huge store of knowledge.
Access to technology narrows the digital divide.
AI and Augmented Reality change how people act and react.
Digital platforms, social media and games serve business and entertainment.

screens.title: Socialization gaps and cyberbullying
paras: Families and friends bond by talking together.
Many devices at home can reduce family socialization (Figure 1.5).
Friends in a cafe may stare at screens instead of talking.
Cyberbullying: sending, posting or spreading hurtful or malicious content about someone online.
It includes disclosing private information to embarrass or humiliate.
It happens on social media, forums, games, texts and messaging apps.
Example: online gender-based violence, harassment and sexual abuse.

screens.title: Social media and gaming addiction
paras: A behavioural addiction: being overly concerned about social media or games.
An uncontrollable urge to log on.
So much time spent that other important life areas suffer.
Intensive online activity can harm young people's mental health.
It affects family relationships, learning, future goals and mental health.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The gap between people who have access to technology and those who do not.
Less natural interaction in families and among friends because each person is busy with a device.
Sending, posting or spreading hurtful or malicious content about someone online, or disclosing their private information to humiliate them.
A behavioural addiction: too much concern for social media or games, an urge to log on, and so much time spent that other life areas suffer.

screens.text: Posting hurtful content about a classmate in a Telegram group is
screens.why: p.6: sending, posting or disseminating hurtful or malicious content about someone online.
screens.clue: Who is being hurt, and where?

screens.title: Which social issue?
items: Sisters sit together but only look at their phones
Friends in a cafe never talk
A fake account shares a girl's private photos
Insulting messages in an online game chat
Cannot stop checking Instagram, even in class
Gaming eight hours a day and skipping homework
screens.why: Gap: less real interaction. Bullying: hurting someone online. Addiction: an urge that harms other life areas.
screens.clue: Is someone hurt, ignored, or hooked?

screens.text: Cyberbullying only happens on social media.
screens.why: p.6: it also happens in forums, games, text messages and other messaging apps.
screens.clue: Think of game chats and SMS.

screens.text: How can too much gaming and social media hurt a student's academic goals?
opts: It takes time from study and sleep and breaks concentration
It has no effect on learning
screens.ans: It takes time from study and sleep and breaks concentration
screens.why: p.7: these habits affect "learning performance, future life goals, and mental health".
screens.clue: What does the time come from?

screens.text: Why has wider access to phones and social media increased cyberbullying?
opts: Bullies can reach victims anytime, and content spreads fast to many people
screens.ans: Bullies can reach victims anytime, and content spreads fast to many people
screens.why: More access means more places to post (p.6), and posts reach large audiences quickly.

screens.text: Which change best improves a student's technology habits?
opts: Set time limits and turn off notifications while studying
Keep the phone in bed at night
screens.ans: Set time limits and turn off notifications while studying
screens.why: Be "curious and mindful" about use (p.7); let technology improve your life, not distract from it (p.6).

screens.text: Abel's private photo is shared in a group chat with mocking comments. He then stays online all night reading replies and misses his exam. Which issues appear?
screens.why: Sharing private photos to humiliate is cyberbullying; an urge to stay online that harms other life areas is addiction.
screens.clue: Look at what others did, then what Abel did.

en.text: The University of Oxford defines plagiarism as presenting work or ideas from another source as your own, with or without the original author's consent, without full acknowledgement. Copying from the Internet is easy, so schools now use tools to check originality. Plagiarism can destroy credibility and lead to dismissal or job loss. Students should produce original work, use sources for insight and credit the authors.

am.text: የሌላን ሰው ሥራ ወይም ሀሳብ ምንጩን ሳትጠቅስ የራስህ አስመስለህ ማቅረብ ፕላጃሪዝም ነው። ሁልጊዜ ምንጭህን ጥቀስ።

screens.title: Is it plagiarism?
screens.ask: Hana copies three paragraphs from a website into her essay without naming the source. The website owner said it is okay. Is it plagiarism?
opts: Yes, because the source is not acknowledged
Only if she copies a whole page
screens.after: Oxford: plagiarism is presenting others' work as your own "with or without consent", without full acknowledgement.

screens.title: Plagiarism
paras: Having access to all knowledge has its own drawbacks.
Oxford: plagiarism is presenting work or ideas from another source as your own.
It counts with or without the author's consent, if there is no full acknowledgement.
Students can easily copy and paste whole passages from the Internet.
Schools now use tools to check the originality of work.
It can destroy credibility and lead to dismissal from school or job loss.

screens.title: Using online sources without plagiarising
steps: Read the source for ideas and insight.
Put any exact words in quotation marks.
Cite the author, title and website in a reference list.

screens.title: Key word
defs: Presenting work or ideas from another source as your own, with or without consent, without full acknowledgement.

opts: Handing in a friend's essay as your own
Quoting a book and naming the author
Listing your sources at the end
screens.ans: Handing in a friend's essay as your own
screens.why: Presenting another person's work as yours without acknowledgement is plagiarism.
screens.clue: Whose work is it, and is it credited?

pool: Use quotation marks for exact words
Copy and paste without a source
Change a few words and claim it
a: Use quotation marks for exact words
screens.why: p.7: use sources as references and "give appropriate credit to authors".

screens.text: Using someone's idea without credit is fine as long as you do not copy their exact words.
screens.why: Plagiarism covers "work or ideas" presented as your own.
screens.clue: Read the definition again: work OR ...

screens.text: According to the book, plagiarism at school or work can lead to
opts: loss of credibility, dismissal from school or job loss
screens.ans: loss of credibility, dismissal from school or job loss

screens.text: Yonas rewrites an article in his own words but names no source. Is it plagiarism?
opts: Yes: the ideas are still presented as his own without acknowledgement
No: paraphrasing never needs a source
screens.ans: Yes: the ideas are still presented as his own without acknowledgement
screens.why: Changing words does not change whose ideas they are; full acknowledgement is still needed.

en.text: Cybercrime is using a computer as an instrument for illegal ends, such as fraud, identity theft or violating privacy and intellectual property. INSA reports that cyber attacks on Ethiopia are increasing, so citizens should protect personal, organisational and national digital resources; skilled students can become cyber warriors. Automation improves service but replaces routine jobs such as cashiers, data entry clerks and factory workers. It often creates as many jobs as it destroys, but they need new skills.

am.text: የሳይበር ወንጀል ኮምፒውተርን ለሕገወጥ ዓላማ መጠቀም ነው። አውቶሜሽን አንዳንድ ሥራዎችን ያስቀራል፤ አዳዲስ ሥራዎችንም ይፈጥራል።

screens.title: Machines and jobs
screens.ask: Automation lets machines do routine work. Over time, what usually happens to the number of jobs?
opts: Automation often creates about as many jobs as it destroys
screens.after: p.9: "Automation often creates as many jobs as it destroys over time." The skills needed keep changing.

screens.title: Cybercrime
paras: Britannica: using a computer as an instrument for illegal ends.
Examples: fraud, stealing identities, violating privacy or intellectual property.
It grows as computers become central to education, commerce and government.
INSA reports that cyber attacks on Ethiopia are increasing.
All citizens and professionals must work together against them.
This is 21st-century patriotism: protecting our digital sovereignty.

screens.title: Cyber warriors
paras: A cyber warrior is a well-trained IT or information security professional.
Cyber warriors manage computer networks and system operations.
Figure 1.9 shows them defending against cyber attacks, beside #ItsMyDam and the GERD.
Interested, skilled students can start this journey.

screens.title: Job opportunities and challenges
paras: AI and automation do routine tasks and improve service.
But some jobs are lost: cashiers, data entry clerks, factory workers.
Automation often creates as many jobs as it destroys.
The skills people need keep changing.
People with low education are most at risk.
The future job market needs more skilled professionals.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Using a computer as an instrument for illegal ends, such as fraud, stealing identities or violating privacy and intellectual property rights.
A well-trained, skilled IT or information security professional who manages computer networks and system operations.
Using machines and systems to do routine tasks that people used to do.

screens.text: Which is an example of cybercrime?
opts: Using a computer to steal someone's identity
screens.ans: Using a computer to steal someone's identity
screens.why: Britannica (p.8): a computer used for illegal ends such as stealing identities.

screens.title: At risk, or created by technology?
screens.why: Routine tasks are automated; new technology needs people to build, run and secure it.
screens.clue: Is the task routine and repetitive?

screens.text: According to INSA reports, cyber attacks on Ethiopia are
screens.why: p.8: they show "increasing trend from time to time".

screens.text: People with low educational backgrounds are most at risk of losing jobs to automation.
screens.why: p.9: they are "most at risk since the future job market needs more skilled professionals".

screens.text: Which skills best prepare you for 21st-century jobs?
opts: Digital literacy, problem solving and lifelong learning
screens.ans: Digital literacy, problem solving and lifelong learning
screens.why: The skills needed keep changing (p.9), so people must keep learning new digital skills.

screens.text: A bank replaces 10 data entry clerks with software but hires 4 IT support staff and 3 data analysts. What does this show?
opts: Automation removes routine jobs but creates new jobs that need new skills
Data entry is a growing job
screens.ans: Automation removes routine jobs but creates new jobs that need new skills
screens.why: Routine work was automated; new skilled roles appeared (p.8–9).
screens.clue: Compare the old jobs and the new ones.
